While its primary meaning is 'male child,' Hebrew idiom uses 'son of X' to mean 'one characterized by X' or 'member of category X'—thus 'sons of the prophets' are prophetic disciples, 'sons of Belial' are worthless people, and 'sons of valor' are warriors. The same construction with numbers expresses age: 'son of thirty years' means 'thirty years old.' This productive phrase structure reveals how Hebrew thinks categorically through kinship metaphors."

'Sons of the prophets' are guild members, 'sons of Belial' are scoundrels. Swahili shifts to watu wa (people of), revealing the categorical function beneath the kinship metaphor.

    Enriched: Male offspring in the direct biological or legal sense, including descendants. This core kinship meaning dominates the usage in genealogies and narratives. Cross-linguistic glosses uniformly use basic words for male child: Spanish hijo, Arabic ابْنَ, Hindi बेटा/पुत्र.
    Existing Spanish translations: a-hijos-de, hijos-de, hijos-de-
